lines.source: old lab film, scene 1, first line
lines.text: An AI can plan a robot's next move. But what if the answer arrives after the moment it was needed?

lines.source: old lab film, scene 1: at sixty hertz the controller gets 16.67 ms, every time
lines.text: A machine that moves runs on a beat. Many times a second, its controller has to act. Not usually. Every time.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 1: inference time is variable; DeadlineModel's slow request takes several controller ticks
lines.text: An AI model keeps a different clock. Most answers come back quickly. Some take far longer, and nobody can say in advance which.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 2: blocking inference delays later jobs too, red squares count missed deadlines
lines.text: Make the controller wait for the model, and one slow answer costs it a beat. Then the next. The delay spills into everything queued behind it.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 2: a separate worker proposes updates and the controller never waits for it
lines.text: So take the model out of the waiting path. The controller keeps its beat whatever happens. The model works beside it and leaves its newest plan.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 3: the loop may stay on time while using an answer about a world that has changed
lines.text: That changes how things fail. Every beat is now on time, but a plan can describe a world that has already moved on.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 3: observation timestamp checked before use, fallback when a proposal expires
lines.text: So every plan carries the moment it was made. If it is too old, the controller sets it aside and falls back to a safe default.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 3: freshness is only one check; validate action limits separately
lines.text: Age is only one check. A fresh plan can still be wrong, so the limits on what the machine may do keep their own guard.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 4 and DeadlineModel: async misses are zero when isolated and appear only under shared stalls
lines.text: One trap remains. If the model and the controller share a computer, a busy model can still steal the controller's time. Keep them apart, and test it under load.

lines.source: old lab film, scene 5 closing line: adopt better intelligence without losing the timing contract
lines.text: Better AI will keep arriving. The question is whether a system can take it in without losing its beat.
